subject: MAP: tradeoff path & region commitment for CardioSync POC
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Tom Barker <tom.barker@cardiosync.com>; Susan Lee <susan.lee@cardiosync.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: tradeoff path & region commitment for CardioSync POC

Hi Tom / Susan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, I’m attaching an updated mutual action plan that focuses on the deployment-mode decision (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and the evaluation milestones we agreed on. The key questions we need to lock this week are:

- Which deployment mode does CardioSync prefer for the initial POC (hosted for fastest time-to-value, dedicated for predictable throughput, or private for data isolation)?
- Which region(s) must we guarantee for latency/compliance (US-east, US-west, EU)?
- Any procurement or legal gating items that will change the timeline?

I’ve sketched a recommended tradeoff path in the MAP: start hosted for the 4-week evaluation, run our latency/throughput tests, and pivot to Dedicated (reserved pool) by the pilot cutover if throughput or data controls require it. If CardioSync requires on-prem or VPC at go-live, we’ll surface the Private deployment plan in week 3 and include a longer lead time.

Attached: CardioSync_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP with milestones, owner matrix, and acceptance criteria). Also included a short SOC2 Q&A extract.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm preferred initial mode + required geo by Thursday EOD (3/4).
2) We provide a targeted config + cost delta for Dedicated and Private by Friday (3/5).
3) Run the perf baseline (Redwood hosted) the week of 3/8 if you greenlight hosted.

If helpful I can schedule a 30-min tech deep-dive with Karthik and our infra team to walk the acceptance criteria and region SLOs.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: CardioSync_MAP_v2.xlsx (xlsx), SOC2-answers.pdf (pdf)

From: Tom Barker <tom.barker@cardiosync.com>

Cc: Susan Lee <susan.lee@cardiosync.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: tradeoff path & region commitment for CardioSync POC

Olga —

Thanks for the write-up and the MAP. Quick answers from our side after internal sync:

- Preferred initial mode: Hosted for the POC (we want the fastest route to validate behavior against real traffic).
- Required region: US-east (primary), but we’d like a US-west fallback for disaster recovery testing.
- Procurement/legal: procurement wants a short statement on data residency and an outline of the Dedicated SLA if we move to reserved capacity.

Also attaching three quick items for your team: our list of sample workloads, expected peak TPS, and a short compliance checklist. We’ll need the SOC2 artifact you mentioned for internal reviewers.

Can we get the Dedicated cost delta by Friday? If hosted performance looks good next week, we’ll aim to sign a reserved commitment by end of Q2.

Tom Barker
VP Engineering | CardioSync Health
tom.barker@cardiosync.com

Subject: RE: MAP: tradeoff path & region commitment for CardioSync POC

Olga / Marissa —

Quick internal note after reviewing CardioSync’s sample workloads (thanks Tom). Two technical flags to call out before we finalize the Dedicated cost delta: 

1) Sequence lengths and KV cache hit patterns look skewed to long-tail conversations — we should suggest quantization + larger KV cache on Dedicated to avoid tail latency.
2) US-east preferred — we can run an identical hosted baseline in us-east and report p50/p95/p99 token latencies. If they require US-west fallback we should schedule cross-region replication testing to measure failover hit to latency (adds ~2 business days).

I’ll draft the perf-test plan and the initial Dedicated config (GPU SKUs, batch size, estimated token/hour) and drop to the MAP spreadsheet by Friday.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

--
Note: add SOC2-answers.pdf to the response pack, and include a short note on retention controls for CardioSync’s procurement team.

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 14:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: tradeoff path & region commitment for CardioSync POC — hosted baseline + delta

Tom / Susan —

Short update per MAP timeline:

- Hosted baseline: we’ve scheduled the perf baseline in us-east for Mon 3/8 and reserved a second window in us-west for DR verification on 3/10. Karthik will run the p50/p95/p99 and share results in the MAP.
- Dedicated delta: estimate attached in the MAP sheet — move from hosted to dedicated adds an estimated 32% unit cost for guaranteed reserved throughput and the larger KV cache; estimated lead time for reserved pool is 2 weeks after contract signature.
- Private (on-prem/VPC): provided a separate gating list — jump to Private increases implementation lead time to ~8–10 weeks and requires KMS integration and network validation.

Next concrete asks from CardioSync: please confirm (by end of next week 3/12) whether you want us to:
A) proceed with hosted-only evaluation and deliver results (fastest path), or
B) include a Dedicated pricing/contract worksheet up front so procurement can review now, or
C) start a parallel Private readiness assessment (longer runway).

I’ve attached CardioSync_MAP_v2.xlsx and SOC2-answers.pdf into the shared Drive link for your procurement/reviewers. I’ll also set up a 30-min tech deep-dive for Monday 3/8 (invite to follow).

—
Olga Petrov
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: CardioSync_MAP_v2.xlsx (xlsx), SOC2-answers.pdf (pdf)
